provenance.quote: City Services/Business License Reform Measure. To protect City of Emeryville services/ensure smaller businesses pay less than larger businesses, shall the measure be adopted to: keep parks/playgrounds safe; repair potholes/maintain streets; maintain 9-1-1 response; improve crime prevention; maintain senior/youth services; general government use; by updating/simplifying Emeryville’s 42 year old business license rates up to 0.4% of gross receipts (described in the ordinance) until ended by voters, providing $12,400,000 annually, requiring independent oversight?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces most of Emeryville’s business-license tax categories with gross-receipts rates beginning January 1, 2027. Ordinary businesses with annual receipts above $100,000 would pay 0.1% for general commerce, retail and utilities; 0.3% for contractors, services and unclassified businesses; or 0.4% for real-property rentals and professional or advanced services. Percentage rates apply to the business’s full taxable receipts. Those at or below the threshold would pay $25 annually. The ordinary annual tax cap rises from $300,000 to $800,000. The threshold and cap adjust annually with the San Francisco–Oakland–Hayward Consumer Price Index from January 1, 2028. Revenue, estimated in the ballot at $12.4 million annually, can fund any lawful city purpose. The ballot specifies independent oversight. It requires majority approval and has no fixed expiration.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the new business-tax categories, rates, small-business threshold, annual cap and calculation rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing business-license tax structure and rates.

parts.label: Business categories and exceptions
parts.what: The 0.1% category includes retailers, restaurants, manufacturing, lodging, salons, childcare and utilities. The 0.3% category includes ordinary services, transportation, warehouses, data centers, contractors and unclassified businesses. The 0.4% category includes property rentals and professional or advanced activities such as software, research, finance, healthcare, media and headquarters. Existing separate cannabis, cardroom and massage-parlor tax rules remain. The $800,000 cap applies to the ordinary annual tax under the gross-receipts section.

parts.label: Taxable receipts and operating costs
parts.what: Tax generally uses the prior calendar year’s receipts apportioned to Emeryville; 2027 uses 2026 receipts. New or newly resumed businesses use estimates, followed by adjustment to actual receipts at renewal. Underpaid tax is due then; overpayments may be refunded or credited at the Finance Department’s discretion. If city-apportioned receipts are lower than the costs of operating in the city, those costs become the receipt measure. Costs include payroll, utilities, rent, insurance, depreciation and other ordinary expenses; remote workers must be assigned an official work location using the ordinance’s criteria.

parts.label: Exemptions and city authority
parts.what: Businesses exempt under federal or state constitutional or statutory law remain exempt to that extent but must demonstrate eligibility and obtain a business-tax certificate. The council may create full or partial exemptions and make amendments that do not require voter approval for a tax increase. The Finance Director administers collection, classifications and apportionment, may issue regulations and may grant up to 30 additional days for filing or payment for good cause.
